chapters.summary: Councilmember Thomas-Henry fills in for Chair Louis, introduces attending members including Carr, Encarnación, Farías, Schulman, Salaam, Sanchez, and notes the agenda: three votes followed by four public hearings on rezoning proposals across Brooklyn, Queens, and the Bronx.
chapters.title: Acting Chair Thomas-Henry introduces members and outlines agenda

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Good morning and welcome to the meeting of the Subcommittee on Zoning and Franchises.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Chair Lewis is unable to attend today's meeting.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: I am Councilmember Thomas Henry and I will serve as acting chair for the subcommittee today.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: This morning, I am joined by Minority Leader

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Councilmember Carr, Deputy Whip Encarnacion, Councilmember Farias, Councilmember Shulman, Councilmember Salam,

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: and online, Councilmember Justin Sanchez, as well as in person, Councilmember Aldebal.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: And Council Member Wilson.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Today we are voting on three proposals and holding four hearings.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The three proposals we will first vote on consist of 4703 108th Street, mixed use residential rezoning in my district.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: 200 Kent Avenue, mixed-use residential rezoning in Councilmember Ressler's district,

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: and the Flatiron Nomad major concession application regarding portions of Broadway and Fifth Avenue in Councilmember Wilson and Epstein's districts.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: We will then hold the hearings on the following proposals.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: 815 Hutchinson River Parkway, rezoning in Councilmember Aldeball's district.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: 862 through 868, Kent Avenue rezoning in Councilmember Ressler's district.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: 158-06 Northern Boulevard rezoning in Councilmember Ung's district.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: And 132 Melrose Street rezoning in Councilmember Gutierrez's district.

chapters.summary: Chair Thomas-Henry explains hybrid meeting format, two-minute testimony limit, email submission process for written testimony, and decorum requirements including no video recording from the witness table.
chapters.title: Testimony rules and meeting format instructions

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: This meeting is being held in hybrid format.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Members of the public who wish to testify may testify in person or via Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Members of the public wishing to testify remotely may register by visiting the New York City Council website.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: At www.council.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Dot NYC dot gov slash land use.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: To sign up or for those of you in person, please see one of the sergeant at arms to prepare and submit a speaker card.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Members of the public may also view a live stream broadcast of this meeting on the council's website.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: When you are called to testify before the subcommittee, if you are joining us remotely, you will remain muted until recognized by myself to speak.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: When you are recognized, your microphone will be unmuted.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: We will limit public testimony to two minutes per witness.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: If you have additional testimony that you would like the subcommittee to consider, or if you have written testimony that you would like to submit instead of appearing in person, please email it to

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: landuusetestimony at council.nyc.gov.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Written testimony may be submitted up to three days after the hearing is closed.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Please indicate the LU number and or project name in the subject line of your email.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: We request that witnesses joining us remotely remain in the meeting until excused by the chair, as council members may have questions.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Lastly, for anyone attending today's meeting, this is a government proceeding and decorum must be observed at all times.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Members of the public are asked to...

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: not to speak during the meeting unless you are testifying.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The witness table is reserved for people who are called to testify and no video recording or photography is allowed from the witness table.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Further, members of the public may not present audio or video recordings as testimony, but may submit transcripts of such recordings to the Sergeant at Arms for inclusion in the hearing record.

chapters.summary: Thomas-Henry presents LUs 118 and 119 for a mixed-use residential rezoning in Corona, Queens with 119 apartments and 30 affordable, recommending modification from R7X to R7D given surrounding low-scale context. She supports the application as modified.
chapters.title: Chair describes 47-03 108th Street rezoning vote item

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: We will now proceed with the three votes.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: And I would also like to add that we have been joined by Councilmember Ressler.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The first vote concerns LUs 118 and 119 regarding 4703 108th Street rezoning proposal in my district.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The applicant is seeking to develop a mixed-use residential development in Corona, Queens that would have approximately 119 apartments, of which approximately 30 would be permanently affordable.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The proposal involves two actions.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The first is a zoning map amendment to change the existing residential R6B district to a residential R7X district with a C24 commercial overlay.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The second action is a zoning text amendment to map mandatory inclusionary housing area and level of affordability, which would be limited to MIH option one.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: We are recommending that the project area be rezoned to R7D rather than an R7X district, given that the surrounding area consists predominantly of two- and three-story buildings.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: I support this application as modified, and we will move on to the next.

chapters.summary: Thomas-Henry presents LUs 115 and 116 for enlarging and converting a commercial building in Williamsburg into 143 apartments with 36 affordable, recommending removal of MIH option 2. Councilmember Restler supports the application as modified.
chapters.title: Chair describes 200 Kent Avenue rezoning vote item

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The second vote concerned LU's 115 and 116 regarding 200 Kent Avenue mixed-use residential rezoning proposal in Councilmember Ressler's district.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Applicant is seeking to enlarge and convert an existing commercial building into a mixed-use residential development in Williamsburg, Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The proposed redevelopment would have approximately 143 apartments, of which approximately 36 would be permanently affordable.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The proposal involves two actions.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The first is a zoning map amendment to change the existing manufacturing M1-4 district to a mixed-use district consisting of a paired M1-4 district with a residential R7X district.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The second action is a zoning text amendment to map a mandatory inclusionary housing area.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: We are recommending one modification to remove MIH option 2, which will require the affordable apartments are provided at an average of 60% AMI.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Councilmember Ressler supports this application as modified.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: I will now turn it over to the councilmember for a statement.

chapters.summary: Restler expresses gratitude to the development team, notes the existing Trader Joe's and commercial space will remain, and praises the project for adding housing above the supermarket. He highlights the developer's partnership with the North Side BID formation effort.
chapters.title: Councilmember Restler on 200 Kent Avenue project

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Justin E. Sanchez
utterances.text: It's good to see you in the seat.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I just wanted to express gratitude to the development team at 200 Kent.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: The developers and their representatives were really great partners through this process.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: This is an existing building.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Many of you may know it.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: We have a Trader Joe's there on the basement level of a five-story building on Kent Avenue that was zoned just for commercial use.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And this is really an area where we have lots of residential development, and allowing for residential development above the dynamic supermarket and existing commercial space is, I think, a very positive thing for our neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: There will be...

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Still more commercial space, multiple stories of it.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So hopefully we can maintain and sustain the office space that's there and then build a mixture of market rate and affordable housing above.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: I'm really pleased by this project.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: The development team is working closely with my office on the bid formation effort that we have on the north side to help improve street cleanliness and quality of life across our commercial corridors and our park spaces and our open streets.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: And I'm really grateful for their partnership in that endeavor.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: So this is, I think, a very sensible project, and I'm really pleased to support it and hope my colleagues will do the same.

utterances.speaker: Lincoln Restler
utterances.text: Thanks so much.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

chapters.summary: Thomas-Henry presents LU 117 to expand the existing Flatiron District concession area to approximately 162,345 square feet, managed by the Flatiron NoMad Partnership, supported by Council Members Wilson and Epstein.
chapters.title: Chair describes Flatiron NoMad major concession vote item

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The third and final vote concerns LU 117 regarding the Flatiron Nomad major concession application for portions of Broadway and Fifth Avenue in Councilmember Wilson's and Epstein's districts.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Over the past few years, there have been temporary initiatives to re-envision this corridor between 19th Street and West...

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: And West 31st Street to create a more engaging and safer public realm for pedestrians and cyclists.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: This application would expand the existing Flatiron District concession area to approximately 162,345 square feet of concession area.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The expanded area will be managed by the Flatiron Nomad Partnership.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Council Members Wilson and Epstein support this application.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: I will now turn it over to Council Member Wilson for remarks.

chapters.summary: Wilson praises the Flatiron NoMad Partnership's 20-year stewardship, noting post-pandemic growth in demand for pedestrianized streets. He highlights expanded revenue for public spaces, cleaning services, compost bins, and potential public bathrooms, thanking colleagues and staff.
chapters.title: Councilmember Wilson on Flatiron NoMad major concession

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: It is a major day to vote on a major concession.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Since its genesis 20 years ago, the Flatiron Nomad Partnership has been an excellent steward of the area, now extending from Flatiron to all of Nomad and 20th Street and 6th Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: The Broadway Corridor, one of the most highly trafficked areas of the city, grew exponentially.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: in a post-pandemic world as demand for outdoor dining, public space activation, and pedestrianized streets amplified, and Flatiron Nomad met and exceeded the expectations of what it could do for the neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: It is my hope that this committee and then tomorrow the whole council will vote a resounding yes on this major concession agreement.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: This agreement will significantly expand the ways the bid can generate revenue that will lead to more beautiful public spaces, expanded cleaning services for the district, and additional smart compost bins.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: It also unlocks the future potential for the installation of public bathrooms and water fountains.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I'm eager to see the ways this agreement transforms the neighborhood for the better.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: I want to first thank my colleague, Councilmember Harvey Epstein, for his partnership and for taking the lead on getting this process started while the council seat was vacant.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And thank you to the bid for all they do to keep our communities beautiful, safe, and prosperous.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And a big thank you to DOT and DSNY for their collaboration and willingness to think constructively about how we can maximize our ability to invest in public spaces.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: And a big thank you to the council land use team, Omar, Chelsea, Arthur, and Dana, especially Dana.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: For supporting this effort and to my chief of staff, Hannah Moses, and legislative and budget director, Jacob Bloomfield, for their hard work on this since day one.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: It's my hope that the partnership can continue its work by preserving and beautifying the landscape along Broadway and beyond.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: and that we can be a meaningful companion in that endeavor.

utterances.speaker: Phil Wong
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Chair Thomas-Henry opens the preconsidered LU hearing for 815 Hutchinson River Parkway, a commercial rezoning in the Ferry Point neighborhood of the Bronx in Councilmember Aldebol's district, seeking to change M1-2 to C8-3 to allow large retail including a supermarket.
chapters.title: Opening of 815 Hutchinson River Parkway hearing

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: We will now move on to the hearings that are scheduled for today.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Beginning with the public hearing on pre-considered LU regarding 1815 Hutchinson River Parkway, a commercial rezoning proposal in the Ferry Point neighborhood of the Bronx in Councilmember Aldeball's district.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The proposal seeks to change an existing manufacturing district to a commercial district to allow large retail establishments of 10,000 square feet and larger at an existing commercial center.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Although there is a target that is larger than 10,000 square feet at the site, it is located below grade and the shops at the street level are limited to stores smaller than 10,000 square feet.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry

chapters.summary: Jarboe of Roth Crew presents the rezoning from M1-2 to C8-3 for the Throg's Neck Shopping Center, explaining the site's location near the Bruckner Interchange and Whitestone Bridge. He details how 1961 M1 zoning restrictions limit retail stores over 10,000 square feet, preventing a supermarket from locating at the center.
chapters.title: Justin Jarboe: 815 Hutchinson River Parkway site location and zoning history

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: When you begin your presentation, please restate your name and organization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Good morning, members of the subcommittee and Councilmember Audible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: My name is Justin Jarboe of Roth Crew, Roth Crew Inspector.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: I'm here today on behalf of MD Hutch Owner, LLC, the owner of the existing Throg's Neck Shopping Center at 815 Hutchinson River Parkway in Bronx Community District 10.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Joining us remotely are Adam Rothkru, zoning counsel for the applicant, and former state senator Jeffrey Klein, along with his associate, Michelle Dalgall.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Possibly also present on behalf of ownership are Danielle Contillo and Aaron Malinsky.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: So we are here in connection with the zoning map amendment that would change the zoning of a single block in which the shopping center sits, bounded by Lafayette Avenue to the north,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Brush Avenue to the west, and Winter Place to the south, and the Hutchinson River Parkway Service Road to the east from M12 to C83.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: The application is sought primarily to expand the range of permitted commercial uses, including the ability to locate a supermarket in excess of 10,000 square feet to serve as an anchor tenant for the upper floor of the shopping center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: This proposal is not sought for an increase in permitted density and no vertical enlargement is sought.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: The bulk height yard and setback regulations of the proposed CA3 district are generally the same as those in the M12 district.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: What we're asking for is that the zoning recognize the commercial character of the shopping center as opposed to a manufacturing use, which restricts certain commercial uses above 10,000 square feet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: In terms of the location of the site, the block to the north is the campus of Bronx Catholic School and Monsignor Scanlon High School.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Further north is a Home Depot.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: The area to the south of Winter Place contains single-family homes interspersed with smaller commercial establishments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: And then further south along Westchester Creek is a series of single-story warehouses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: To the east across the Hutchinson River Parkway is St.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Raymond Cemetery, and of course to the west is Westchester Creek.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: The site sits just south of the Bruckner Interchange, where the Cross Bronx and the Bruckner Expressways meet, and immediately north of the Whitestone Bridge.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: It is a regional retail location, fronting a limited access parkway, and has functioned as one since the center opened in 2013.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: This slide shows the location of the underlying M12 zoning district against Westchester Creek and the residential districts that surround it.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Dating back to 61, the applicable provisions of the zoning resolution have prohibited certain retail uses in excess of 10,000 square feet in M1 districts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: The 1961 regulations, which remain in effect today, allow toy, hardware, drug, book, office supply stores of any size,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: while food, furniture, clothing, department stores, variety, and floor covering and appliance stores are limited to 10,000 square feet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: The nature of retail development has also changed dramatically since 1961, while the restriction has not.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: COVID in particular changed retail habits with online shopping, reducing foot traffic for certain retailers, recognizing the importance of flexibility for a shopping center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Importantly, retailers like grocery stores remain quite active, as most shopping is still preferred in person, and can serve as an active tenant to bring foot traffic to a larger shopping center, which in turn supports the adjacent businesses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: However, based on the current M1 zoning, a supermarket cannot be located within the center today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: A use that has repeatedly indicated is needed, it wouldn't be very desirable for this location.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: As a matter of background, this block was zoned M1-2 at the inception of the 1961 zoning resolution when the area was more industrial in character with warehouses lining Westchester Creek.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: It subsequently sat vacant until it was approved with the shopping center in 2013.

chapters.summary: Jarboe shows the proposed C8-3 zoning boundary coterminous with the shopping center parcel, noting no density increase is sought. He describes existing conditions: 410,000 square feet of development, 875 parking spaces, and current tenants including Target (below grade), TJ Maxx, Petco, Applebee's, and the NY Blood Center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: And given the size of the shopping center, there is no plan or reasonable expectation that the property will be used for manufacturing use.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Sorry, here we show the existing M12 and the proposed CA3 district, as well as the boundary of the rezoning area, which is coterminous with the shopping center parcel.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: We're not proposing to rezone any property we do not own, and no other lots are affected.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: The C8 district is intended as a bridge between commercial and manufacturing uses where large amounts of land are typically required, which describes this nearly eight acre site.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: The change to C83 would appropriately allow a wider array of, I should say, a wider variety of stores at excessive 10,000 square feet, including a supermarket.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: If you could skip ahead to slide nine, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: So these photographs show the existing conditions along each frontage, Lafayette Avenue, Brush Avenue, Winter Place, and the Hutchinson River Parkway Service Road.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: The site contains about 410,000 square feet of development, of which only about 100,000 is actually zoning floor area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: So it has the floor area of 0.28.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: The building rises to a maximum height of 37 feet, and it provides about 875 parking spaces, 606 of which are located on the rooftop or the upper floor of the structure, and about 10 loading berths.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Current tenants include a Target as the anchor tenant on the lower floor, which is located below grade and as a quirk in the zoning does not count as zoning floor area and is therefore permitted as of right.

chapters.summary: Jarboe explains the proposed 30,000 square foot grocery store on the upper floor requiring a 10,000 square foot addition, with no specific grocer identified yet. He addresses Winter Place traffic concerns, describing a proposed Lafayette Avenue left-turn solution blocked by DOT's pending bike lane plan, and notes Community Board 10 and the Bronx Borough President recommended approval.
chapters.title: Justin Jarboe: proposed grocery store and Winter Place traffic mitigation

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: The upper floor is developed with a TJ Maxx, a Petco, an Applebee's, a Chipotle, five guys at Starbucks, and several smaller retail outlets, as well as a location for the New York Blood Center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: If you could go to slide 12, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: So this is an illustrative depiction of the development that would take place to facilitate a new grocery store, which would be located on the upper floor.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: It would involve about 10,000 square foot addition on that floor to accommodate a 30,000 square foot grocery store and will involve about a reduction of 49 parking spaces.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: However, there's about 800 parking spaces that would remain and would be sufficient to accommodate parking at the shopping center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: I will note that no grocery store operator is identified at this time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: As a specific store will not sign a lease and undertake the large capital investment until the zoning is in place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: I'll also note that no specific store is being replaced or displaced at this time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: When the application commenced, there was a larger party city store that had gone out of business, and that space was identified as a likely location for a supermarket.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: However, because of the length of the application, during that time, that space was leased with the New York Blood Center.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: So if and when this application is approved, ownership will explore a location within the center for a supermarket, which is most likely the area shown in red on these plans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: In regards to traffic, if you could go back to slide three.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Yeah, it's the aerial.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Just the next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Great, thanks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Before I close, I want to address Winter Place because traffic has been a concern along that roadway.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: Neighbors on Winter Place have experienced the use of their street by commercial traffic leaving the center and heading to Brush Avenue due to a mandatory right turn out of Lafayette Avenue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: So we took that concern seriously and engaged in discussions with the Department of Transportation and retained an engineering firm to prepare plans showing the creation of a new left turn out of Lafayette Avenue across an existing traffic island, thereby redirecting traffic away from Winter Place.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: However, upon meeting with Bronx DOT, we were advised that a cut through along Lafayette would not be possible because of a proposed safety plan that includes a new bike lane along Lafayette Avenue, which has not yet been finalized.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: In the event that plan is not implemented, we're happy to revisit the creation of a cut through.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: And in the meantime, ownership will continue to notify its tenants to direct their suppliers away from Wenter.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: And remains open to discussing how to address any ongoing traffic problems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: I should note that based on the extensive traffic studies performed as a part of this application in the EAS, and given the absence of a substantial increase in square footage,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: The addition of a supermarket is not projected to have a noticeable impact on winter place in terms of new traffic.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: I'll also mention, as you mentioned before, Community Board 10 overall voted in favor of the application, and the Bronx Borough President also recommended approval.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Justin Jarboe
utterances.text: So I think that concludes our presentation, and our larger team is available to answer any questions you might have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: And as I mentioned, three of the five tax lots are proposed to be redeveloped.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: Those three tax slots measure about 20 feet in width each, totaling a lot of about 6,300 square feet.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: The current zoning is M11.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: As I previously mentioned, the proposed rezoning area is comprised of five tax lots.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: In addition to the rezoning from M11 to a proposed M1, from M11 to an M1-2A slash R6A, which is an MX district, we're also proposing a zoning tax amendment to map all five tax lots

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel

chapters.summary: Mandel shows 1940s images of residential buildings on the five lots, noting three were demolished by the 1970s. He presents current photos showing the two lots used for parking and loading, the two-story warehouse building, adjacent non-conforming residential uses, and a six-story office building on Evergreen Street.
chapters.title: Ron Mandel: historical residential uses and current site photos

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: which serves as warehouse space and office above, and the other two tax lots are used for parking and loading.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: The lots are conveniently located within walking distance to mass transit, the J and Z lines, as well as New York City bus routes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: Next.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: The purpose of the aerial map depicted on the screen is to demonstrate this unique M11 pocket in this Bushwick neighborhood.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: The site, which is outlined in orange, is on the south side of Melrose Street, right across from the Denizen building, which we'll talk about in another few minutes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: As you can see from the aerial map,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: Much of the block already is occupied by residential uses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: The surrounding uses range from eight to nine story mixed use residential buildings directly across from the other street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: That's the Denizen building, which is the result of the Rheingold rezoning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: And other two to five story warehouse and commercial buildings, as well as two to five story residential buildings at the mid block.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: Next.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: Touching upon the council member's comment before about the building across the street, that's the building located on the left in the photograph on the screen, referred to as the Denizen Building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: It's a nine-story residential building, which substantially changed the composition and character of this portion of Melrose Street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: The building was constructed in 2019, and since then has been proven to be a very difficult challenge for our client to operate their business across the street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: The Melrose Street itself measures about 50 feet in width.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: Once you subtract the sidewalks and parking on both sides of the street, there's only 11 feet of width located on that street.

chapters.summary: Noriega explains the M1-1 district mapped since 1961 doesn't reflect the area's predominantly residential character. After consulting with the councilmember and community board, an MX district was chosen to maintain industrial uses. The proposed 3.9 FAR building would have 25,000 square feet, predominantly residential with light manufacturing on the ground floor.
chapters.title: Frank Noriega: MX district rationale and development plans

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: As you can imagine, it's extremely difficult to not only back a trailer in, which they used to be able to do years ago, but also even to park a truck along the street to unload goods for both goods coming in and goods coming out.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: In addition to that, it's compounded by substantial traffic, which was expressed by the community board along this portion of Melrose, as well as substantial pedestrian traffic, which again makes it unsafe now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: To have these trucks parked on the street.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: The client who's been in the neighborhood now for 17 years operating their business has located with their 24 employees, which are substantially from the surrounding neighborhood, to a warehouse building around the corner at 6 Stanwix.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: They're really excited about that space.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: It's actually appropriately configured to allow for loading, unloading, parking,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: storage

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: alongside a loading berth, as well as a freight elevator in that building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: Just quickly, next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: We thought this was interesting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: The five lots actually were occupied at one point by residential uses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: These are images from the 1940s of those multifamily residential buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: On the right side are the two nonconforming residential buildings, which still exist today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel

utterances.text: By the 70s.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel

utterances.text: And these are images from the 1980s tax map.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: Next.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: Some photos of the project site.

chapters.summary: Noriega describes dividing the 6,000 square foot ground floor into two smaller spaces for light manufacturing such as maker spaces, furniture making, or coffee roasters, based on feedback from the Evergreen Exchange. He outlines sustainability features including green roofs, all-electric appliances, heat pumps, energy-efficient lighting, and low-flow plumbing fixtures.
chapters.title: Frank Noriega: light manufacturing space and sustainability features

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: Upper left is an image of the site.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: The two lots are used for parking and loading.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: The two-story building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: To the right, another image of the two adjacent nonconforming residential uses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: On the bottom left is an image of Evergreen Street to the west, occupied by a six-story office building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ron Mandel
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: And just to reiterate, so what we're trying to do here is rezone from the M11 district that has been mapped there since 1961.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: And as Ron pointed out in the prior slides, this really hasn't really been a manufacturing area.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: It was actually predominantly residential until it was demolished, and now it's mostly vacant sites.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: We proposed specifically the MX district after consulting with a council member.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: Originally, we were looking at a potential commercial district because, as was mentioned before, it's really difficult to get trucks down on this site now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: But after discussing this with the council member and the...

chapters.summary: Thomas-Henry asks why the rezoning is limited to five lots. chapters.title: Chair questions on rezoning area scope and industrial use retention

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: Input from the community board, it is desirable to maintain some sort of industrial uses here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: And as I see we're running out of time, I'm just going to touch briefly on the next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: There's been a couple of different reviews of this area and have noted similarly that they want to maintain industrial uses in this area, but they also note that

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: There has been a long story.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: standing non-conforming residential uses here that need to be addressed, but there's also a need for affordable housing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: So our goal is to balance all of these issues together and propose a development that meets all of the needs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: Go to the next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: Actually, we'll skip over this one and just kind of touch on what ends up here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: Our proposed development site will end up being a 3.9 FAR building, which is effectively just under 25,000 square feet,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: predominantly residential, 18,000 square feet, and specifically we're looking to have some sort of light manufacturing of some sort on the ground floor level.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: Next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: After discussing this with both the community board as well as groups like the Evergreen Exchange, we found that there is a need or a desire for some sort of small space.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: As shown here, we have divided this 6,000 square foot ground floor into two smaller spaces to allow for potential

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: Light manufacturing, when we talk light manufacturing, we're talking maker spaces, maybe small furniture stores or furniture making stores, coffee roasters or something.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: And we're looking to incorporate that into the ground floor after community feedback.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: And next slide, please.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: Another issue that's been come up, both of the committee board as well as the council member, is the idea of efficiency in the buildings.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: And under the new codes, as a new development, we're going to be required to do more efficient buildings, and we're proposing green roofs as well as all the new appliances in these buildings will be electric.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: So the sustainability fix here is going to be much more ideal than what would be for a normal manufacturing building.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega
utterances.text: That would currently be allowed on site.

chapters.summary: Thomas-Henry relays Gutierrez's questions about securing a light industrial tenant. utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Frank Noriega

utterances.text: I do have a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: So this application includes only a few lots in an M1 block that has existing residential uses and vacant lots.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Why was the zoning lot restricted to only five lots?

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The rationale for that was that the project site is the three tax lots, and we incorporate the two adjacent lots, which are occupied residentially, just to bring them into conformance.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: After working with the council person and city planning, we thought it was appropriate to only rezone the five tax lots so that there's not, so as the potentially the lot did get redeveloped,

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: there'd be a better understanding as to what the proposed uses would be on the block.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The idea behind the MX was that it would set basically

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: It would be, how can I explain it?

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The MX district then, the idea behind it was that in the future, if adjacent owners wanted to rezone their property, and if the lot itself was wide enough to accommodate manufacturing use, then that MX could be dragged further west.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: And to add to that, it's particularly closer to Evergreen Street.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The studies such as the Bushwick plan had looked at that site and along Evergreen and it's also seen in the Rheingold development that there might be a potential for a higher density residential along Evergreen.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: So the discussion there should be set for a different, it would be a potentially higher like an R7A district, which is not what we're proposing here.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: We're doing a lower density on the side street of an R6A, which would be a smaller building.

utterances.text: And what are the current industrial uses on the site, and will they be offered?

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Space in the new building.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: The families that own the property and also operate the business conduct electric part distribution.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: They already have located to a more appropriate facility around the block with their 24 employees.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Okay, so they won't come back.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: They'll just use it.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: The applicant confirms no studios will be included in the building, is open to working with a local organization to market MIH units, and details energy-efficient systems including heat pumps, green roofs for stormwater absorption, electric appliances, energy-efficient lighting, and low-flow plumbing fixtures, though no solar panels are planned.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: And I do have a couple of questions from Councilmember Gutierrez.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: When a mixed-use district is proposed in place of a manufacturing district, it is important that we retain industrial use while introducing residential as it helps retain jobs that have been an integral part of this community.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: I appreciate your current plans include light industrial on the ground floor.

utterances.text: So in our process, I mean, we've been marketing this with brokers and whatnot to see if there are some sort of light manufacturing.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: We have been getting some response for that.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: But particularly with the discussions with the Evergreen Exchange, there has been a strong desire for a space like this, but they need space now.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: So it's similar to what I think other projects have said.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: We haven't tenanted a space or a specific tenant yet, but we anticipate that it will be.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: But the big discussion which we tend to commit to is that

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Because even if we do go forward, if they don't have the height on the ground floor, they need higher floor to ceiling heights generally for industrial uses.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry

summary: Subcommittee on Zoning and Franchises votes 7-0 to approve three land use items: 47-03 108th Street rezoning (with modifications), 200 Kent Avenue rezoning (with modifications), and Flatiron NoMad major concession expansion.

Four preconsidered land use hearings held: 815 Hutchinson River Parkway commercial rezoning (Bronx), 862-868 Kent Avenue residential rezoning (Brooklyn), 158-06 Northern Boulevard residential rezoning (Queens), and 132 Melrose Street residential rezoning (Brooklyn).

Public testimony on 158-06 Northern Boulevard reveals community division between residents citing traffic and neighborhood character concerns and supporters calling for more affordable housing in Flushing.
